question: In India, which vegetation has dominating species i.e., teak and sal?
solution:
The correct answer is** __Tropical Deciduous Forests__**__.__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Tropical Deciduous Forests**

 
 
• ​In India, **Tropical Deciduous Forests **has dominating species i.e., **teak**, **sal** and **shisha**.
 
• In regions with significant yearly **rainfall** followed by a definite** dry season**,** tropical deciduous forests** develop.
 
• These **forest **formations are **dense **and **lush **in the **wet summers**, but they become a bleak scene in the** dry winters** when most of the trees lose their leaves.
 
• Tropical deciduous forests grow in warm, year-round conditions that occasionally get several hundred centimetres of rain.
 
• They have long dry seasons that can extend for several months.
 
• Tropical deciduous forests are often found in two bands, one between 10° and 20°N latitude and the other between 10° and 20°S latitude.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tropical Thorn Forests and Scrubs**

 
 
• The **tropical Thorn forests and Scrubs** are a type of forest or area that receives too little or inadequate rainfall, with an average annual total of less than 70 cm. Typically, they can be found in India's semi-arid states of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, and the dry **Deccan Plateau regions.**
 
 
 
• **Mangrove Forests**
 
 
• ​**Mangrove forests** are fertile wetlands that grow in **coastal intertidal zones**.
 
• They are also known as mangrove swamps, mangrove thickets, or mangals. Due to mangroves' inability to survive subfreezing temperatures, mangrove forests are primarily found in **tropical and subtropical latitudes.**
 
 
 
• **Tropical Evergreen Forests**
 
 
• ​A forest with **evergreen trees** is known as an **evergreen forest.**
 
• Conifers and holly in frigid regions, eucalyptus, Live oak, acacias, magnolias, and banksia in more moderate zones, and rainforest trees in **tropical zones** are just a few examples of the diverse range of trees that may be found in these **ecosystems**.
